note: Attacker-controlled RAR5 file bytes are read into p via the client callback; the variable-sized integer encoding is the first parsed input.
raw_hdr_size is decoded from the attacker-controlled varint; it determines the total header size and thus the layout of all subsequent fields.
header_id is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; value 0x02 selects HEAD_FILE, routing execution to process_head_file.
hash_type is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; its value influences the file header parsing path.
flags is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; bit 0x04 (HFL_EXTRA_DATA) controls whether extra_area_size is read and extra data is parsed.
extra_area_size is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; it determines the size of the extra data region that follows the fixed file header fields.
Inside the extra-data loop, the extra field ID is decoded; value 0x06 selects EX_UOWNER, routing to parse_file_extra_owner.
flags is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; bit 0x01 (OWNER_USER_NAME) causes user_name_len to be read and user_name to be filled.
user_name_len is decoded from attacker-controlled bytes; a value of 257 exceeds OWNER_MAXNAMELEN (256).
user_name points to attacker-controlled bytes of length 257; these bytes will be copied into the stack buffer.

snprintf with size=256 writes up to 255 bytes plus a null terminator; when user_name is 257 bytes, the null terminator is written at offset 256, which is one byte past the end of the 256-byte stack buffer.
Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 (null byte) at offset 256 into user_name_buf[256]; this is the memory-safety sink.
